mainTopic: שניות (their counting, scope, and application to converts), converted brothers as witnesses, and the new משנה on who counts as a brother or son for יבום
overview: The גמרא finishes counting the list of שניות. It then rejects רב הלל's proof against אמימר, because no one can confirm that the list he saw was written by מר בריה דרבנא. Next comes a teaching from the school of רבי חייא that adds great-granddaughters and the wife's great-grandmothers as שניות. The גמרא explains why the wife is counted as a generation going up but not going down. It then asks whether these שניות have a stopping point; both proofs are pushed off, and the question is never settled. רב נחמן teaches that the רבנן did not decree שניות for גרים, and he rules on whether converted brothers may testify together, where אמימר is more lenient. The גמרא explains that testimony is in the hands of בית דין, and a גר is like a newborn. Finally, a new משנה teaches that any brother obligates יבום and any son exempts from it. The גמרא shows that 'of any kind' includes a ממזר, and it begins an argument that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Two similar cases count as one, so the total is sixteen
steps.stepSummary: Two relatives on the list that are alike are counted as a single item, which brings the total to sixteen.
steps.simpleTranslation: Those two that are similar to each other are counted as one, and so there are sixteen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא settles a counting problem from the earlier discussion. Two similar relatives on the list of שניות are counted as one item, so the list comes out to sixteen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two relatives are the wife of the father's father's brother and the sister of the father's father. Both are the same kind of relative, one generation up from a forbidden relative. Grouping them as one item makes the number on the list fit.

keyTerms.meaning: that are similar to each other

phrases.english: Those two that are similar to each other
phrases.notes: These are the father's father's brother's wife and the father's father's sister from the earlier discussion.

phrases.english: he counts them as one,
and so there are sixteen.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנָךְ תַּרְתֵּי דְּדָמְיָין לַהֲדָדֵי כַּחֲדָא חָשֵׁיב לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves a counting problem raised earlier on the daf about the list of שניות.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Grouping two similar cases into one item
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The number of items on the list does not seem to match the stated total.
steps.terutzMaskana: The two similar relatives count as one, giving sixteen.

steps.title: רב הלל insists he saw them written as forbidden
steps.stepSummary: רב הלל restates his challenge: whatever the count, he personally saw these relatives written as forbidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: But in any case, I myself saw them written as forbidden!
steps.whatsHappening: רב הלל pushes back against אמימר's lenient view. He says that whatever the count is, he saw these relatives listed as forbidden with his own eyes.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The counting question was only one part of the debate. רב הלל's real point is eyewitness evidence: a written list (said to be from מר בריה דרבנא) forbids these relatives. That would contradict אמימר, who permitted them.

keyTerms.meaning: in any case; no matter what

phrases.english: But in any case,
I myself saw them
phrases.notes: The speaker is רב הלל, repeating the claim he made earlier against אמימר.

phrases.english: that they are written as forbidden!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָא מִכׇּל מָקוֹם לְדִידִי חַזְיָין לַן דִּכְתִיבָן לְאִיסּוּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Puts the counting aside and goes back to the main challenge against אמימר.
steps.kashyaTarget: אמימר's ruling that these relatives are permitted
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A written list that רב הלל saw lists them as forbidden, which contradicts אמימר.

steps.title: רב אשי: an unsigned list proves nothing
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי answers that the list carries no signature of מר בריה דרבנא, so it cannot be relied on either way.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: By your logic, if it had been written as permitted, would you have relied on it? Is מר בריה דרבנא signed on it? So now too, when it is written as forbidden, מר בריה דרבנא is not signed on it.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי rejects רב הלל's evidence. Since nobody can confirm who wrote the list, it cannot be used to overturn אמימר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי turns the question around: if the list had said 'permitted,' רב הלל would not have trusted it without proof of authorship. A source that would not count as proof for leniency cannot count as proof for strictness either. So אמימר's ruling stands.

keyTerms.meaning: and according to your own reasoning
מר son of רבנא, the supposed author of the list

steps.whatToRemember: A written source of unknown authorship cannot be used to overturn a known authority's ruling, whether the source is strict or lenient.

phrases.english: He said to him: And according to your reasoning,
phrases.notes: רב אשי is answering רב הלל.

phrases.english: if it had been written as permitted,
would you have relied on them?

phrases.aramaic: דְּמָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבְנָא מִי חֲתִים עֲלַיְיהוּ?
phrases.english: Is מר son of רבנא signed on them?
Now too, when it is written as forbidden —

phrases.aramaic: לָאו מָר בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַבְנָא חֲתִים עֲלַיְיהוּ.
phrases.english: מר son of רבנא is not signed on them.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: וְלִיטַעְמָיךְ, אִי הֲוָה כְּתִיב לְהֶיתֵּירָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the evidence brought in step 2.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects the written list as proof against אמימר
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Nobody can verify who wrote the list, so it has no authority in either direction.

steps.title: School of רבי חייא: great-grandchildren and the wife's great-grandmothers
steps.stepSummary: A teaching from the school of רבי חייא lists more שניות: the third generation down from one's own children and from the wife's children, and the fourth generation up from the in-laws.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי חייא taught: The third generation from his son, from his daughter, from his wife's son and from his wife's daughter is a secondary forbidden relative. The fourth generation from his father-in-law and from his mother-in-law is a secondary forbidden relative.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a teaching from the school of רבי חייא. The teaching adds great-granddaughters going down, and the wife's great-grandmothers going up, to the list of שניות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going down, the teaching says 'third' (great-granddaughter). Going up, it says 'fourth,' because the wife herself is counted as the first generation. This difference in counting sets up the next question.

keyTerms.meaning: the school of רבי חייא taught
a secondary forbidden relative, forbidden by the רבנן

phrases.english: The school of רבי חייא taught:
The third generation of his son and of his daughter,
and of his wife's son and of his wife's daughter — is secondary.
The fourth generation of his father-in-law and of his mother-in-law — is secondary.
phrases.notes: This means his wife's great-grandmother, counting the wife herself as the first generation.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins a new topic about which generations are included in שניות.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Great-granddaughters (one's own and the wife's) and the wife's great-grandmothers are שניות.

steps.title: רבינא asks why the wife is counted only going up
steps.stepSummary: רבינא asks רב אשי why the wife is counted as a generation going up ('fourth') but not going down ('third').
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said to רב אשי: Why is it that going up he counts his wife, and going down he does not count his wife?
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא points out an inconsistency in how the teaching counts generations. He asks for the reason, which the גמרא gives in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Going up, the teaching counts the wife and says 'fourth.' Going down, it does not count her and says 'third.' רבינא wants to know why the same counting method is not used in both directions.

phrases.english: רבינא said to רב אשי:
What is different going up,
that he counts his wife,
and what is different going down,
that he does not count his wife?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבִינָא לְרַב אָשֵׁי: מַאי שְׁנָא לְמַעְלָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Questions the counting method used in step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the wife is counted as a generation going up but not going down.

steps.title: Going up, the prohibition comes through the wife
steps.stepSummary: The wife is counted going up because those women are forbidden only through her. Going down, the descendants are his own relatives, so she is not counted.
steps.simpleTranslation: Going up, where the prohibition comes through his wife, he counts her. Going down, where the prohibition does not come through his wife, he does not count her.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: the wife is counted only when the relationship runs through her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: His wife's great-grandmother is related to him only through his wife, so the wife counts as a link in the chain. His own great-granddaughter is his blood relative, so the wife is not part of the chain and is not counted.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַעְלָה, דְאִיסּוּרָא מִכֹּחַ אִשְׁתּוֹ קָא אָתֵי —
phrases.english: Going up, where the prohibition comes through his wife —
he counts her;

phrases.aramaic: לְמַטָּה, דְאִיסּוּרָא לָאו מִכֹּחַ אִשְׁתּוֹ קָאָתֵי —
phrases.english: going down, where the prohibition does not come through his wife —
he does not count her.

steps.triggerLanguage: לְמַעְלָה, דְאִיסּוּרָא מִכֹּחַ אִשְׁתּוֹ קָא אָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבינא's question from step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The wife is counted only when the prohibition comes through her.

steps.title: But the wife's own descendants also come through her
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects: the wife's son's and daughter's descendants are forbidden through the wife, yet she is not counted there.
steps.simpleTranslation: But his wife's son and his wife's daughter, where the prohibition comes through his wife, and he does not count her!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer in step 6. It points to a case in the same teaching where the prohibition comes through the wife, but the wife is still not counted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching says 'third' for the wife's son's and daughter's line too, not 'fourth.' Those descendants are related to him only through his wife, so by the rule in step 6 she should have been counted.

phrases.english: But his wife's son and his wife's daughter,
where the prohibition comes through his wife,
and he does not count her!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the rule given in step 6.
steps.kashyaTarget: The rule that the wife is counted whenever the prohibition comes through her
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The wife's own descendants are forbidden through her, yet the teaching still says 'third' and does not count her.

steps.title: The wording was kept the same for both lines going down
steps.stepSummary: Because the teaching already said 'three generations below him' without counting the wife, it used the same wording for the wife's line.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since he taught three generations below himself and did not count her, he also taught three generations below her and did not count her.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Going down, the teaching kept one uniform wording for both his line and his wife's line.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For his own descendants, the wife really is not counted. Right next to that, the teaching describes the wife's descendants in the same style ('third') so the wording stays parallel. The rule from step 6 still holds; this case is only an exception in wording.

keyTerms.meaning: since; because it already (said one thing)

steps.whatToRemember: Going up, the wife is counted because the relationship runs through her. Going down, the teaching says 'third' for both lines just to keep the wording uniform.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not conclude that the wife's descendants are his blood relatives. The relationship still comes through the wife; only the style of counting matches his own line.

phrases.aramaic: אַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא שְׁלֹשָׁה דּוֹרוֹת לְמַטָּה דִּידֵיהּ
phrases.english: Since he taught three generations below himself
and did not count her,

phrases.aramaic: תְּנָא נָמֵי שְׁלֹשָׁה דּוֹרוֹת לְמַטָּה דִּידַהּ
phrases.english: he also taught three generations below her
phrases.notes: 'Her' here is the wife: her own descendants from her son or daughter.

phrases.english: and did not count her.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַיְּידֵי דִּתְנָא שְׁלֹשָׁה דּוֹרוֹת לְמַטָּה דִּידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from step 7 and keeps the rule from step 6.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the wife's descendants come through her, the teaching should have said 'fourth.'
steps.terutzMaskana: The teaching said 'third' only to keep its wording parallel with his own descendants.

steps.title: Do the extra secondary relatives of רבי חייא's school have a stopping point?
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי asks רב כהנא whether the שניות from the school of רבי חייא stop at the generation named, or continue on forever.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said to רב כהנא: The שניות taught by the school of רבי חייא, do they have a stopping point, or do they not?
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי asks a new question about the list from Step 4. Is only the named generation forbidden, or does the איסור keep going to further generations?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 4 said 'third generation' and 'fourth generation.' רב אשי wants to know whether the איסור ends exactly there (it has a הפסק) or keeps going up or down without end (it has no הפסק).

keyTerms.meaning: Secondary forbidden relatives, forbidden by the רבנן rather than the תורה
A stopping point: the איסור ends at a certain generation
The school (study hall) of רבי חייא

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רַב אָשֵׁי לְרַב כָּהֲנָא:
phrases.english: Rav Ashi said to Rav Kahana:
The secondary relationships of the school of Rabbi Chiya,
phrases.notes: These are the extra cases from Step 4: the third generation down and the fourth generation up.

phrases.english: do they have a stopping point
or do they not have a stopping point?

steps.triggerLanguage: יֵשׁ לָהֶן הֶפְסֵק אוֹ אֵין לָהֶם הֶפְסֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new question about the scope of the list from Step 4.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the איסור on the third and fourth generations stops there or continues to further generations.

steps.title: Proof from רב: only four women have a stopping point
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from רב's statement that only four women have a הפסק, so these cases would have none.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, for רב said: Four women have a stopping point, and no more.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings an earlier statement of רב to try to answer the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב said exactly four women have a הפסק. 'And no more' suggests every other שניה has no stopping point. That would include the cases of רבי חייא's school.

phrases.english: Come and hear, for Rav said:
Four women have a stopping point,
and no more.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attempts to answer the question of Step 9.
steps.raayaObject: That the שניות of רבי חייא's school have no הפסק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב's statement that only four women have a הפסק.

steps.title: רב may have meant only one particular list
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: רב may have been speaking only about a specific teaching, not about רבי חייא's cases.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps when רב said this, he was referring only to that particular teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the proof from רב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב's 'four and no more' may count only within the list he was discussing. So it says nothing about the extra cases from רבי חייא's school.

keyTerms.meaning: Perhaps: a typical opening for pushing off a proof
A teaching of the תנאים, here a ברייתא

phrases.english: Perhaps when Rav said this
he was referring to that particular teaching.
phrases.notes: He means the list רב was discussing. The extra cases from רבי חייא's school were not part of it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 10.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Only the proof is rejected. The question remains open.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: רב's count may be limited to one list and not cover רבי חייא's cases.

steps.title: Proof from the wording 'third and fourth'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא tries to prove from the teaching itself that the איסור stops at the third and fourth generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'the third and the fourth.' The third and the fourth, yes. More than that, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now looks at the exact words of רבי חייא's teaching to answer the question.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The teaching names specific generations: third and fourth. If every generation were forbidden, why name a number? So it seems only those generations are forbidden, meaning there is a הפסק.

phrases.english: Come and hear: "the third and the fourth."
phrases.notes: This quotes the teaching from Step 4.

phrases.english: The third and the fourth, yes;
more than that, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second attempt to answer Step 9, after the first proof was rejected.
steps.raayaObject: That the שניות of רבי חייא's school have a הפסק.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The exact wording 'third and fourth' in the teaching.

steps.title: It may mean from the third and fourth onward
steps.stepSummary: The proof is pushed off: 'third and fourth' may mark where the איסור starts, not where it ends.
steps.simpleTranslation: Perhaps it means from the third generation onward, and from the fourth generation onward.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא rejects the second proof. The question is left without an answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Naming 'third' could mean 'starting from the third.' Then every generation after it is forbidden too. The wording fits both readings, so it proves nothing.
steps.whatToRemember: The question of whether רבי חייא's שניות have a הפסק is never settled. Both proofs are pushed off.

phrases.english: Perhaps it means from the third onward,
and from the fourth onward.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects the proof of Step 12 and leaves the question open.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The proof is rejected, and the question stays unresolved.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: 'Third and fourth' may mark the starting point, not the end point.

steps.title: Did the רבנן decree secondary relatives for converts?
steps.stepSummary: רבא tells רב נחמן about a question asked in ארץ ישראל: do שניות apply to גרים?
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: Did the master see this scholar who came from the West and said, 'They asked in the West: Did the רבנן decree שניות for גרים, or did they not?'
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins. רבא passes on a question from ארץ ישראל about whether שניות apply to גרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גר is treated as if newly born, with no family ties. So the question is whether the רבנן's extra איסורים of שניות also cover a גר's relatives from before he converted.

keyTerms.meaning: 'The West,' meaning ארץ ישראל (west of בבל)

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
Did the master see this one of the Rabbis
who came from the West and said,
They asked in the West:
Did they decree secondary relationships for converts,
or did they not decree secondary relationships for converts?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new topic, still about שניות, now as they apply to גרים.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether the רבנן's decree of שניות applies to converts.

steps.title: No שניות for converts: a קל וחומר
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the רבנן forbade even real עריות for a גר only for one reason, so they surely did not add שניות.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Now, even for an ערוה itself, if not for the worry that converts would say 'we came from a stricter holiness to a lighter holiness,' the רבנן would not have decreed against it. Is it even a question about שניות?!
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא's question with a קל וחומר. The answer is no: there are no שניות for גרים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: By תורה law a גר has no family ties, so even his close relatives are permitted. The רבנן forbade them only so gentiles-turned-Jews would not say Judaism is less holy than what they had before. That reason is about real עריות, so there is no reason to go further and add the extra layer of שניות.

keyTerms.meaning: A close relative forbidden by the תורה
Is it even a question? (meaning: obviously not)

steps.whatToRemember: For a גר, even the real עריות are only forbidden by the רבנן, to prevent a bad impression. So שניות are not decreed for גרים at all.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that a גר's family איסורים rest on one specific reason. A גזירה is not stretched beyond the reason behind it.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הַשְׁתָּא וּמָה עֶרְוָה גּוּפַהּ,
phrases.english: He said to him: Now, if regarding a forbidden relationship itself,
phrases.notes: רב נחמן doesn't answer whether he saw the scholar. He goes straight to the question.

phrases.english: were it not for "so that they should not say
we came from a stricter holiness to a lighter holiness,"
phrases.notes: As gentiles these relatives were forbidden to them, so being permitted as Jews would look like a step down.

phrases.english: the Rabbis would not have decreed against them;
is it even a question about secondary relationships?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 14.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The רבנן did not decree שניות for גרים, proven by a קל וחומר from the עריות themselves.

steps.title: רב נחמן: converted brothers as witnesses
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן rules that maternal brothers who converted should not testify together, but their testimony counts if they did. Paternal brothers may testify together from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב נחמן said: Since we are discussing converts, let me add a ruling. Converted brothers from the same mother should not testify together, but if they did, their testimony is valid. Converted brothers from the same father may testify together from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן uses the topic of גרים to add a new ruling about testimony.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Relatives normally cannot testify together, but a convert's old family ties do not count in the eyes of the law. The mother's side is treated a bit more strictly, since the רבנן already treated it more seriously for עריות. So it is avoided from the start, but it is not invalid after the fact. The father's side is not seen as real family for non-Jews at all.

keyTerms.meaning: if they already testified (after the fact)

phrases.english: Rav Nachman said:
Converts, since they have come into our hands,
phrases.notes: He means: since we are already talking about converts (from steps 14–15).

phrases.english: let us say a ruling about them:
Brothers from the same mother should not testify together,
but if they did testify, their testimony is valid.
Brothers from the same father may testify together from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: גֵּרִים, הוֹאִיל וַאֲתוֹ לְיָדָן, נֵימָא בְּהוּ מִלְּתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from converts and שניות to converts and testimony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Converted maternal brothers should not testify together, but it is valid after the fact. Converted paternal brothers may testify together from the start.

steps.title: אמימר: even maternal brothers may testify
steps.stepSummary: אמימר says that even converted maternal brothers may testify together from the start.
steps.simpleTranslation: אמימר said: Even brothers from the same mother may testify together from the start.
steps.whatsHappening: אמימר disagrees with רב נחמן and is more lenient.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב נחמן made one small restriction, on maternal brothers from the start. אמימר removes it completely. In his view, a convert has no family ties at all for testimony.

phrases.english: Ameimar said:
Even brothers from the same mother also
may testify together from the start.

steps.triggerLanguage: אַמֵּימָר אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ אַחִין מִן הָאֵם נָמֵי מְעִידִין לְכַתְּחִלָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Argues with רב נחמן's restriction on maternal brothers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Converted maternal brothers may also testify together from the start.

steps.title: Why is testimony different from forbidden relations?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why converts are treated leniently for testimony, when the רבנן were strict with them about עריות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how is this different from forbidden relations?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the lenient rulings about testimony. It sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With עריות, the רבנן did forbid a convert to marry some of his old maternal relatives. So the old family ties seem to matter there. Why should they not matter for testimony too?

phrases.english: And how is this different from forbidden relations?
phrases.notes: This points back to step 15, where the רבנן forbade some real עריות for a גר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the lenient testimony rulings by comparing them to the strict rule for עריות.
steps.kashyaTarget: The leniency for converted relatives testifying together.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If old family ties count for עריות by rabbinic decree, they should count for testimony too.

steps.title: Relations are handled by everyone, testimony by the court
steps.stepSummary: Everyone deals with עריות, so a decree was needed there. Testimony is handled by בית דין, which knows the difference. And a convert is like a newborn.
steps.simpleTranslation: Forbidden relations are handed over to everyone. Testimony is handed over to the court. And a convert who has converted is like a newborn child.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by pointing out who is in charge of each area.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every person decides for himself whom to marry. So the רבנן worried people would get confused and made a decree. Testimony is judged by בית דין, which will not get confused, so no decree was needed. The basic law stays in place: a convert starts fresh like a newborn, with no family ties.

keyTerms.meaning: handed over to; in the hands of
a convert is like a newborn child

steps.whatToRemember: A convert is like a newborn, so his old family ties do not count. The רבנן were strict about עריות only because everyone handles those, and people might get confused. Testimony is in the hands of בית דין, so there is no worry.

phrases.english: Forbidden relations are handed over to everyone,
testimony is handed over to the court,
and a convert who converted is like a newborn child.

steps.triggerLanguage: עֶרְוָה — לַכֹּל מְסוּרָה, עֵדוּת — לְבֵית דִּין מְסוּרָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 18.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Testimony should be as strict as עריות for converts.
steps.terutzMaskana: The עריות decree was made because everyone handles marriage. Testimony is run by בית דין, so the basic rule applies: a convert is like a newborn.

steps.title: משנה: any brother obligates יבום
steps.stepSummary: The משנה teaches that a brother of any kind obligates his dead brother's wife in יבום and is his brother in every way. The exception is a brother born from a שפחה or a גויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Whoever has a brother of any kind, that brother obligates his brother's wife in יבום, and he is his brother in every way. The exception is someone whose brother was born from a Canaanite maidservant or from a non-Jewish woman.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins. It defines who counts as a brother for יבום.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'of any kind' mean that even a brother with a flawed status still counts. Only a child born from a שפחה or a גויה is not a brother in the eyes of the law, because such a child takes the mother's status.

keyTerms.meaning: of any kind; in any case

phrases.aramaic: מַתְנִי׳ מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אָח מִכׇּל מָקוֹם —
phrases.english: משנה: Whoever has a brother of any kind,
that brother binds his brother's wife to יבום,
and he is his brother in every way,
except for one who has a brother
from a Canaanite maidservant or from a non-Jewish woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ אָח מִכׇּל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new משנה, unrelated to the testimony discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any brother obligates יבום, except one born from a שפחה or a גויה.

steps.title: משנה: any son exempts from יבום
steps.stepSummary: A son of any kind exempts his father's wife from יבום. He is liable for striking or cursing his father and is his son in every way, except a son born from a שפחה or a גויה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Whoever has a son of any kind, that son exempts his father's wife from יבום. He is liable for striking his father or cursing him, and he is his son in every way. The exception is someone whose son was born from a Canaanite maidservant or from a non-Jewish woman.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה continues with the same pattern, this time for a son.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A man who leaves any son has not died childless, so his widow needs no יבום. The same son is fully a son for other laws too, like the death penalty for striking or cursing a parent. A son from a שפחה or a גויה is not considered his son at all.

phrases.aramaic: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בֵּן מִכׇּל מָקוֹם —
phrases.english: Whoever has a son of any kind,
that son exempts his father's wife from יבום,
and he is liable for striking him and for cursing him,
and he is his son in every way,
except for one who has a son
from a Canaanite maidservant or from a non-Jewish woman.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִי שֶׁיֵּשׁ לוֹ בֵּן מִכׇּל מָקוֹם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second half of the same משנה, with the same pattern applied to a son.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Any son exempts from יבום and is a full son, except one born from a שפחה or a גויה.

steps.title: What does 'of any kind' add?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what extra case the משנה's words 'of any kind' come to include.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: 'Of any kind' comes to include what?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins discussing the משנה by asking about one phrase in it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'of any kind' seem extra. They must be there to include some brother we might have thought does not count.

phrases.english: גמרא: 'Of any kind' comes to include what?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about a phrase in the משנה.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which case the word מכל מקום comes to include.

steps.title: רב יהודה: it includes a ממזר
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה says 'of any kind' includes a ממזר.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יהודה said: It comes to include a ממזר.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יהודה answers that the phrase includes a brother who is a ממזר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even though a ממזר has a flawed lineage, he is still a brother. So he obligates his brother's widow in יבום.

keyTerms.meaning: child born from a forbidden union, with a flawed lineage

phrases.english: Rav Yehuda said:
It comes to include a ממזר.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: מכל מקום includes a ממזר brother.

steps.title: Isn't that obvious?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that a ממזר is obviously a brother, so why say it?
steps.simpleTranslation: That's obvious! He is his brother!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב יהודה's answer as too obvious to need saying.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A ממזר really is the son of the same father. So it seems the משנה did not need extra words to include him.

phrases.english: That's obvious, he is his brother!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב יהודה's answer as obvious.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב יהודה's reading that מכל מקום includes a ממזר.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ממזר is clearly a real brother, so there is no need for a special word to include him.

steps.title: We might have learned from יעקב's sons
steps.stepSummary: One might have learned 'brother' from בני יעקב, who were all of proper lineage. That would leave out a ממזר, so the משנה teaches that he counts.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might have said: Let us learn the word 'brother' here from the word 'brother' used for בני יעקב. Just as there they were of proper lineage and not flawed, so too here only brothers of proper lineage count. So the משנה teaches us otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains why the ruling about a ממזר is not obvious after all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Torah calls בני יעקב 'brothers', and they all had proper lineage. Through a גזירה שוה, we might have limited 'brother' in יבום the same way. The phrase 'of any kind' blocks that idea, so a ממזר is a full brother.
steps.whatToRemember: A ממזר is a full brother for יבום. The words 'of any kind' in the משנה stop us from limiting 'brother' to people of proper lineage, the way בני יעקב were.

phrases.english: You might have said,
let us learn 'brother' and 'brother' from the sons of Yaakov:
phrases.notes: This refers to the פסוק where יעקב's sons call themselves brothers (בראשית 42:13).

phrases.english: just as there, they were of proper lineage and not flawed,
so too here, only those of proper lineage and not flawed;
so it teaches us otherwise.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַהוּ דְּתֵימָא, לֵילַף אַחְוָה אַחְוָה מִבְּנֵי יַעֲקֹב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the 'obvious' challenge of step 24.
steps.terutzResolutionType: מהו דתימא: showing the ruling was needed to block a mistaken reading
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A גזירה שוה from בני יעקב would limit 'brother' to those of proper lineage, leaving out a ממזר.
steps.terutzMaskana: מכל מקום teaches that a ממזר is a full brother for יבום.

steps.title: Maybe a ממזר brother really doesn't count
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we don't simply accept the idea that a ממזר is not considered a brother for יבום.
steps.simpleTranslation: And why not say that this is really the law, that a ממזר brother does not count?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last step. It asks: why not say a ממזר really is not a 'brother' for יבום?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 25 the גמרא said one might learn 'brother' from בני יעקב, which would leave out a ממזר. Now it asks why that mistaken-sounding idea isn't simply the true law. The גמרא needs a reason to reject it.

keyTerms.meaning: And let me say, a way of suggesting another possibility
So it is indeed, this really is the law
A child born from a forbidden relationship, such as עריות

phrases.english: And say that this is indeed so?
phrases.notes: He means: maybe a ממזר brother really does not obligate his brother's widow in יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the תירוץ of step 25 by asking why its 'mistaken' idea should not be accepted as the real law.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that a ממזר must count as a brother for יבום.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If 'brother' is learned from בני יעקב, who were all of proper lineage, perhaps a ממזר truly is excluded, so why should the משנה reject that?

steps.title: A ממזר son does exempt from יבום
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins its answer: since a ממזר son exempts his father's widow from יבום, a ממזר is fully counted for יבום matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: Since, regarding יבום, a ממזר son certainly exempts the widow...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts answering by pointing out that a ממזר son does exempt a widow from יבום. This is a setup: the sentence is not finished, and the conclusion comes on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה in step 21 says a son 'of any kind' exempts his father's widow from יבום, and the גמרא takes it as given that this includes a ממזר son. Step 23 was about a ממזר brother, not a son. The גמרא is building an argument: if a ממזר counts for exempting, he should also count as a brother who creates the obligation. That second half, and the source for the exemption, come on the next amud.

keyTerms.meaning: With regard to, in the matter of
Levirate marriage, a brother marrying his childless brother's widow
Exempts, frees someone from an obligation

steps.confusionAlert: Here the ממזר is the dead man's son, who exempts the widow. The question was about a ממזר brother, who would obligate her. The גמרא is comparing the two roles.

phrases.english: Since with regard to levirate marriage
he certainly exempts [her],
phrases.notes: Literally 'exempting, he exempts.' A ממזר son of the dead man frees the widow from יבום.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins answering the קשיא of step 26 by comparing a ממזר's power to exempt with his power to obligate.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Logical comparison (what is true for exempting should be true for obligating), continued in the next lines.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: A ממזר brother might not count as a brother, since 'brother' is learned from בני יעקב.
steps.terutzMaskana: Since a ממזר son exempts from יבום, a ממזר is counted for יבום, so he should also count as a brother who obligates (finished in the next lines).
